outcome: No change since 26 January 2024: still only two known Wieferich primes (1093, 3511), the search bound (a third must exceed 2^64, established by PrimeGrid in December 2022) has not been extended, and the infinitude question remains open and unproven. Several 2024-2026 papers study Wieferich-type conditions in number fields and function fields, but these are different (variant) problems, not the base-2 rational Wieferich prime question stated in this bullet.
summary: The stated question — whether there are infinitely many (base-2) Wieferich primes, i.e. primes p with p^2 dividing 2^(p-1) - 1 — remains completely open. As of the frozen revision and as of today, only two Wieferich primes are known (1093, discovered 1913; 3511, discovered 1922). The most recent search milestone, PrimeGrid's completion of a combined Wieferich/Wall-Sun-Sun search to 2^64 (~1.8x10^19), establishing that any third Wieferich prime must exceed that bound, occurred in December 2022 — before the frozen revision's date and thus not a change within the window; PrimeGrid has stated it has no plans to continue the search. I found no extension of that search bound and no new example in the 26 January 2024 - present window. Per §3.1, an infinitude question is not advanced by a larger verified search limit even when one exists (and here none post-dates the window at all), so this would not change the status even if a newer bound existed. I found several 2024-2026 papers that touch 'Wieferich' but all address different (related, not case-of) problems under §3.1: (1) arXiv:2508.08472 (Fellini-Murty, submitted Aug 2025, revised Feb 2026) proves, conditional on Masser's abc-conjecture for number fields, infinitude of certain non-Wieferich prime ideals in real quadratic number fields tied to the Ankeny-Artin-Chowla and Mordell conjectures — a number-field generalization, not the rational base-2 question. (2) arXiv:2607.15305 (Niedbala Giraudin, July 2026) exhibits a counterexample to a conjecture of Thakur about Carlitz-Wieferich primes in function fields (degree-5 irreducible c-Wieferich prime over F_19^3), verified independently via Magma (a computer algebra system) by Thakur — a wholly different (function-field, Carlitz-module) analogue, and no AI system was involved (Magma is CAS, not AI). (3) arXiv:2605.13460 (Jones, May 2026) relates classical Wieferich primes to monogenicity of a family of trinomials — a reformulation/application, not a case of the infinitude question. (4) arXiv:2412.11588 (Dec 2024) on Wieferich primes for Drinfeld modules is likewise a function-field analogue. None of these change what a careful person would write in this bullet, none report AI involvement of any kind (no LLM, no AlphaEvolve/FunSearch-style system found in connection with Wieferich primes), and OEIS A001220's most substantive 2025 update (Jianing Song, June 2025) is an algebraic-number-theory remark about Z[2^(1/k)] rather than any advance on infinitude. I am satisfied this is a genuine 'nothing happened' case for the stated question, with the caveat that I cannot rule out an obscure preprint I did not surface.
competing_reading: One could argue the number-field generalization (arXiv:2508.08472) or the AAC/Mordell-conjecture connection is 'about' Wieferich primes closely enough to count, since it uses the same congruence condition and even proves infinitude results — but it proves infinitude of a structurally different object (prime ideals satisfying a generalized non-Wieferich condition in real quadratic fields, conditional on abc for number fields) rather than saying anything about the base-2 rational primes 1093/3511 and their kin. Per §3.1 this is a related/variant problem (changed hypotheses and ambient ring), not a restriction of the stated question, so it does not count as partial progress.
what_would_settle_it: A resolution of the base-2 rational question would require either an unconditional proof of infinitude of Wieferich primes, an unconditional proof of finiteness, or (short of full resolution) a proof of infinitude conditional on a named, well-regarded conjecture (analogous to how abc implies infinitude of non-Wieferich primes) — none of which has appeared for the base-2 case in the window.
